title: Linked List Cycle
oneLinerQuestion: Determine if a linked list contains a cycle using two pointer technique.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Linked List Cycle problem asks whether a singly linked list contains a cycle, meaning a node's next pointer points back to a previously visited node. While tracking visited nodes in a Hash Set solves this in O(N) time, it incurs O(N) memory overhead. Floyd's Cycle-Finding Algorithm (the Tortoise and Hare algorithm) achieves cycle detection in O(1) auxiliary space by deploying two pointers moving at different velocities: a slow pointer advancing one node per step and a fast pointer advancing two nodes per step. If the list is acyclic, the fast pointer reaches null; if a cycle exists, the relative distance between them closes by exactly one node each cycle iteration, guaranteeing an eventual collision inside the loop.

- Step 1: Base Case & Edge Checking — If `head === null` or `head.next === null`, a cycle cannot exist because there are fewer than two linked nodes, so we immediately return `false`.

- Step 2: Pointer Initialization — We initialize two pointer references at the head of the list: `let slow = head` and `let fast = head`.

- Step 3: Fast-Runner Boundary Guard — We execute a while loop guarded by the fast pointer and its immediate successor: `while (fast !== null && fast.next !== null)`. This prevents null reference exceptions when dereferencing the fast pointer.

- Step 4: Advancing Pointers at Differential Speeds — Within each iteration of the loop, we advance the pointers simultaneously: `slow = slow.next` (1 step) and `fast = fast.next.next` (2 steps).

- Step 5: Collision Check — After advancing, we compare the references: `if (slow === fast) return true`. If the two pointers reference the exact same node memory address, the fast pointer has caught up to the slow pointer from behind, confirming the presence of a loop.

- Step 6: Loop Exit & Termination — If the while loop terminates because `fast === null` or `fast.next === null`, the fast pointer reached the end of an open, acyclic linked list, and we return `false`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) where N is the total number of nodes in the linked list; if a cycle of length C exists, the fast pointer catches the slow pointer within at most C iterations once both enter the loop. Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary space because traversal operates exclusively with two pointer references without allocating additional memory.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION hasCycle(head):
    slow = head, fast = head
    WHILE fast IS NOT NULL AND fast.next IS NOT NULL DO:
        slow = slow.next
        fast = fast.next.next
        IF slow == fast THEN RETURN True
    END WHILE
    RETURN False
END FUNCTION
